bull.b: Sustained sequential growth indicates expanding operating activity and improving commercial traction across Soluna’s computing infrastructure. Continued revenue increases can support greater utilization of renewable-powered sites and provide a foundation for scaling hosting, mining, and future AI services.

Conditional Base Load status can protect access to already studied interconnection capacity and reduce a major development bottleneck for large computing loads. This strengthens Soluna’s ability to advance Texas projects and convert its renewable-powered pipeline into operating infrastructure.

The expanded Bitdeer relationship validates demand for Soluna’s site, power, and turnkey operating platform while allowing a major partner to supply equipment. This model can improve utilization and scale computing capacity with less direct hardware ownership by Soluna.

bear.b: Very low gross margins and deeply negative operating results show that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable earnings. Persistent losses limit internally funded expansion and leave profitability exposed to utilization, operating costs, and project ramp timing.

Negative operating and free cash flow means the current business is consuming capital rather than funding its own expansion. Continued burn can constrain flexibility, increase dependence on external financing, and make successful project execution more important to long-term financial stability.

The decline demonstrates that Soluna’s proprietary mining revenue remains sensitive to deteriorating hash-price economics. Shifting capacity toward hosting may diversify revenue, but it also shows that direct mining profitability is not yet a dependable foundation for durable earnings.
